info.name: AI Sentinel Backend - Phases 1 to 10
info.description: Smoke tests for health, PostgreSQL persistence, target ownership/scope, assessment lifecycle, sensitive-test approval gating, owner-scoped evaluations, evidence-linked findings, reports, and retest lifecycle. Evaluation and scanner runs require separately configured workers. Set baseUrl to the local API and enable the development-only identity adapter. Protected requests use X-Development-User; never use this adapter outside local development.

item.name: Phases 4-7 - Assessment, findings, and approval gate
item.description: API lifecycle test: creates an independent repository target, assessment, owner attestation, durable job, verifies that approval cannot be supplied before the workflow reaches its sensitive-test gate, then cancels the queued job. Keep the persistent worker stopped for this folder; use the separate Offline dependency scan folder to test worker execution.

request.description: Expected HTTP 201. This target is separate from the Phase 3 target archived earlier in this collection.
Expected HTTP 201 and status DRAFT. Coverage remains untested until the assessment is started and processed by the separate worker.
Expected HTTP 200 and status READY. approved_by is derived from X-Development-User.

Expected HTTP 202 with job status QUEUED and progress 0. When the separate persistent worker is running with the same data store, it picks up the job and runs supported repository-only Gitleaks assessments.

exec: pm.test('Returns accepted queued job', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(202); });

request.description: Expected HTTP 200. The job can be QUEUED, RUNNING, WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL, or terminal depending on worker progress; repeat this request to observe updates.

Expected HTTP 409 because this regular repository-only fixture is not WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL. In a worker-enabled flow, submit the same body only after the job pauses before an explicitly authorized active/domain test; the owner receives HTTP 200 and the job is re-queued for resume.

item.name: Passive domain check
item.description: Set domainUrl to the HTTPS origin of a domain you own or are explicitly authorized to assess. Run these requests in order with `python -m ai_sentinel.jobs.worker_cli --watch` already running in a separate terminal; it automatically processes queued DOMAIN_ONLY checks. This is one passive HEAD request only: no crawl, redirects, payloads, or active scan.

request.description: Set domainUrl first to an authorized HTTP(S) origin with no path. Target registration records scope only and does not itself authorize a scan.

item.name: Offline dependency scan - OSV Scanner
item.description: Optional flow for Python and Node.js dependency scanning. Configure the pinned OSV Scanner image and fresh local npm/PyPI databases before starting the worker. The scanner container has no network access.

request.description: Run after registering a repository target. Expected HTTP 201 and status DRAFT.

exec: pm.test('Creates dependency assessment draft', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(201); });

request.description: Expected HTTP 200 and assessment status READY.
Expected HTTP 202 and job status QUEUED. With the persistent worker and OSV database configured, the assessment should progress through RUNNING to COMPLETED.
Repeat until status is COMPLETED or FAILED. A missing or stale local OSV database results in assessment errors, not a clean scan.

exec: pm.test('Returns dependency job progress', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description: Run after the job is terminal. A successful offline dependency scan has tool_name osv-scanner and status PASS or FAIL; ERROR means the scan did not complete validly.

exec: pm.test('Returns dependency scan test results', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

item.name: Static analysis scan - Semgrep
item.description: End-to-end Semgrep SAST test. Before running, replace semgrepRepoOwner and semgrepRepoName with a GitHub repository accessible to the configured GitHub MCP worker; semgrepRepoRef defaults to main. Start the persistent worker with a digest-pinned Semgrep image configured. Requests in this folder create and authorize a static-analysis-only assessment, queue it, then expose the scanner test, coverage, and findings. Semgrep currently analyzes Python files only; unsupported languages are reported NOT_TESTED, not PASS.

request.description: Set semgrepRepoOwner and semgrepRepoName to a real GitHub repository accessible to the configured GitHub MCP server before sending. This request is guarded and will not be sent while either value is empty or still a placeholder. Expected HTTP 201.

item.name: Phase 8 - Evaluation results
item.description: Evaluation results are created only by internal code with fixed synthetic cases and an explicitly configured DeepEval model adapter; no public create/run endpoint exists. Run listing/detail tests verify read access only. Cross-tenant rejection is covered by backend tests because the development identity adapter maps all users to one tenant.

request.description: Expected HTTP 200 and a list. It is empty until an internal evaluation worker records a run. If present, the latest result ID is saved to evaluationRunId.

item.name: Phase 9 - Findings and reports
item.description: Findings are derived from deterministic, evidence-linked test results. Reports are generated from persisted assessment records, include coverage gaps and limitations, and never claim that a clean assessment proves security. Finding detail/evidence requests skip if no finding exists yet.

request.description: Expected HTTP 200. Summary totals must match the returned persisted tests and findings. Reports with no tests/findings still include coverage gaps and the clean-report disclaimer.

item.name: Phase 10 - Retesting
item.description: Run only after the original assessment has completed and the finding is confirmed. Set the collection variable retestReady to true after starting the persistent worker with the same shared data store; verify its status at /health/worker.

request.description: Expected HTTP 202 when the owned finding is confirmed, its completed assessment authorization is still valid, and quotas allow the new job. Response includes a new assessment_id/job_id, retest_of_finding_id, retest_of_assessment_id, and status QUEUED. The worker must complete a passing verification scanner before the original finding becomes REMEDIATED_VERIFIED.
